title: Only 1 in 3 doctors trusts insurers' prior authorization promises — AMA 2025 survey report

history.reason: Read to check whether the 2024 burden persisted and to capture reform counterevidence (issue #7)

source_type: industry association article reporting its own physician survey (n=1,000, 2025)
reliability: Same publisher and advocacy caveats as the 2024 survey report; useful as a second annual data point from the same instrument family.
findings: Physicians complete on average 40 prior authorizations per week, consuming about 13 hours of physician and staff time — essentially unchanged from the 2024 survey.
40% of physicians employ staff dedicated solely to prior authorization tasks.
32% reported prior authorization requests are often or always denied.
Only 5% reported health plans offering exemption ('gold card') programs based on physician performance.
Only one in three physicians believes the insurers' 2025 streamlining pledge will produce meaningful change.
limitations: Same self-report and advocacy limitations as the 2024 survey.
Measures physician perception of insurer pledges, not measured process outcomes.
